about.title: About Me
about.bio1: I started out repairing and building computers, and that led me to programming. I trained in systems and networks first, then in application development with Python.
about.bio2: Today I'm at NTT DATA's Innovation Center, where we turn ideas into AI proofs of concept that run in real spaces and on real devices. I work across the stack: React, FastAPI, Azure and the AI agents behind them.
about.motto: I learn best by building something that works.

featured.name: Agentic Space Demo
featured.context: NTT DATA Innovation Center. Lead developer, Dec 2025 - present
featured.description: A digital signage platform driven by AI agents. You upload your content, the AI understands it, builds a story with it, spreads it across the screens of a space and starts it. All of it can be done by talking to an assistant.
featured.problem: Preparing a client visit to the Innovation Center was manual: picking videos and slides, deciding what goes on each screen and setting them up one by one. It took time and depended on someone who knew how to do it.
approach: Every upload is processed automatically: videos are transcribed with Whisper, images described, text pulled from PDFs and PowerPoints, and everything indexed with embeddings to search by meaning.
An orchestrator with specialist agents writes the visit script and decides what each screen shows based on its size and orientation.
The assistant asks just three one-click questions (where, which screens and when) and changes nothing until you confirm the plan.
An interactive floor plan with every screen in its real position, its live status and the route of the visit.
AI spend control: every call is charged to a person's budget, with limits and approvals.

featured.name: Stand Allocation Optimizer
featured.context: NTT DATA Innovation Center. PoC built with a teammate, Jun - Sep 2026
featured.description: A proof of concept that uses machine learning and mathematical optimisation to decide which stand each aircraft parks at and to coordinate its movement on the ground. An operations console loads a full day of flights, detects conflicts, explains them and solves them.
featured.problem: Assigning stands at a large airport leads to overlaps, blocked pushbacks and crossings on the taxiways. The goal was to see the whole day at a glance, find the conflicts and propose a better plan.
approach: A geospatial data pipeline with OpenStreetMap: the real stand inventory and taxi routes computed with Dijkstra.
A stand optimiser with OR-Tools (CP-SAT), built together with my teammate: it reassigns stands to remove conflicts and use fewer remote positions.
Conflict detection on taxiways and runways, and an optimiser that sequences aircraft movements with bounded holds.
The operations console in React: a satellite map (Mapbox), a 3D view in Three.js and a D3 Gantt chart, all driven by the same clock. Plus the Azure deployment with Docker and Terraform.
The machine learning model that predicts each aircraft's time at the stand was built by my teammate.
